## Complete hardness proof
The exact fixed-root, destination-dependent path-cost arborescence problem is strongly NP-hard. The reduction from 3SAT uses a simple depth-three DAG, nonroot indegree at most three, and binary nonnegative costs. Every vertex is root-reachable. The optimum is exactly the minimum number of unsatisfied clauses.

A constant objective offset also gives hardness with strictly positive costs in {1,2}. The proof covers every feasible arborescence, not only trees selected by the reduction.

## Independent adversarial validation
- PASS_COMPLETE_STRONG_NP_HARDNESS_PROOF, with no corrections
- 57,135 submitted assertions replay byte-identically on 449 formulas and 12,696 arborescences
- Independent unfiltered enumeration checked 222,114 edge subsets across 114 formulas, including 1,674 actual arborescences; 14,397 assertions passed
- Frozen proof and eight independent-review files are included unchanged
- The exact original OWR Problem2 and the classical 3SAT source were checked

Record 30003998 duplicates this target and receives no separate attempt or PR. The distinct all-roots Problem1 / 30003996 uses a related literal-selection mechanism; that shared idea is credited rather than presented as an unrelated discovery. Historical priority remains unestablished, and the work has not undergone human peer review.

See unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30003997/README.md and PROOF.md. The proof's submission-time pending header is superseded by the completed review and release metadata. One proof family was used. The coordinating task owns queue updates.
title: 30003997: strong NP-hardness for binary-cost depth-three arborescences
